question: The points $A(1,2)$, $B(4,6)$ and $C(k,10)$ form a triangle of area $6$ square units. Determine all possible values of $k$.
explanation:
Step 1: Write the determinant formula
The given area condition gives $$\frac{1}{2}\left|\begin{vmatrix}1&2&1\\4&6&1\\k&10&1\end{vmatrix}\right|=6$$
Step 2: Expand the determinant
The determinant is $$1(6-10)-2(4-k)+(40-6k)$$
Step 3: Simplify
This becomes $$-4-8+2k+40-6k=28-4k$$ Therefore, $$\frac{1}{2}|28-4k|=6$$
Step 4: Solve the resulting equation
We obtain $|28-4k|=12$. Thus, $28-4k=12$ or $28-4k=-12$.
Step 5: Find the values
The two equations give $$k=4\quad\text{or}\quad k=10$$ Hence, both $4$ and $10$ are possible.
